findings.text: Gzip entry validates container framing around a deflate payload. It accepts only a recognized two byte signature and deflate method, rejects encrypted continuation or reserved flag combinations, skips optional timestamp extra name and comment sections according to flag bits, drives payload decompression, then requires trailer checksum and length to match observed output, signalling failure otherwise.

Deflate stream driver initializes window and bit accounting state, then processes blocks until a terminal flag is observed. It records peak table allocation across blocks, invokes a platform watchdog hook when configured, realigns input to a byte boundary by discarding surplus lookahead, flushes remaining window contents, and propagates block level failures.

Block dispatcher consumes a terminal marker plus a two bit selector from the bit stream and selects one of three decoding paths for stored fixed or dynamic content. A reserved selector is treated as malformed. Input exhaustion during selector fetch yields a distinct underrun outcome, and global bit state is preserved across the dispatch.

Stored block handling requires byte alignment before interpreting a length field and inverted copy, failing when the pair disagrees. Payload bytes are appended to a sliding window with wrap and output flush at capacity, and window plus bit state are restored on success. Exhausted input produces an underrun result rather than partial success.

Fixed block handling builds literal with length decoding structures and distance decoding structures from hard wired code length assignments and lookup sizes, decodes until end of block, and releases all allocated tables on every exit path. Allocation failure and decode failure are reported with distinct outcomes.

Dynamic block handling interprets small header counts with fixed biases to size literal distance and code length alphabets, validates the resulting sizes, reconstructs code length assignments through a border ordering, decodes full length sequences using repeat symbols for runs and zero runs with bounds checks, builds literal and distance decoders with configured lookup sizes, then decodes until end of block with cleanup on all paths.

Window back reference copying must distinguish overlapping from non overlapping ranges. A fast bulk move is permissible only when separation covers the chunk length under unsigned ordering, otherwise elementwise copying preserves overlapping semantics. Reaching window capacity triggers output flush and wrap, and trace output may observe copied bytes.

Decompression routines share window position and bit buffer state through save and restore of locals around each phase. Successful paths write back position and buffered bits, while input exhaustion abandons the update and returns a dedicated underrun code that callers propagate.

Checksum state combines a lookup table with 256 entries and a running register that starts with all bits set so it can reside in zeroed storage. The externally compared checksum value is the bitwise complement of the running register.

Table construction derives an exclusive or pattern from a fixed set of polynomial exponents, seeds the zero entry, then iterates over all byte values shifting through a nine bit augment to populate remaining entries, finally initializing the running register. The routine is designed to permit residence in read only storage with runtime initialization.
The symbol ASCII_FLAG carries value 0x01, CONTINUATION carries 0x02, EXTRA_FIELD carries 0x04, ORIG_NAME carries 0x08, COMMENT carries 0x10, ENCRYPTED carries 0x20, and RESERVED carries 0xC0.

Container framing expects a two byte signature with first byte octal 37 and second byte octal 213 or octal 236, plus method number 8 for deflate. The trailer holds a four byte checksum followed by a four byte original length, each ordered from least to most significant byte.

Fixed decoding uses 288 literal lengths where indices below 144 carry 8, below 256 carry 9, below 280 carry 7 and remainder carry 8, plus 30 distance lengths carrying 5, with lookup sizes 7 and 5. Dynamic headers encode literal count as 257 plus five bits, distance count as 1 plus five bits and code length count as 4 plus four bits, with upper bounds 286 and 30, a border alphabet of 19 entries and a 7 bit tree lookup. Repeat symbol 16 extends prior length for 3 plus two bits, 17 emits zero run of 3 plus three bits and 18 emits zero run of 11 plus seven bits.

Span iteration exposes initialization over a cached tree with first and last bounds, forward stepping to the next hole or used extent, and repositioning to a new index with fast paths for remaining inside the current extent or advancing by one. All three operations act on caller provided iterator state.

Span iteration alternates between hole and used extents and terminates with a distinct flag. Initialization reports a leading hole, a starting used extent, or a whole span hole when no node overlaps. Stepping converts hole to used with bound clamping, emits trailing hole when no successor remains, otherwise emits interior hole and precomputes the following used run. Advancing beyond the upper bound terminates, staying inside adjusts the start, stepping by one moves once, otherwise restarts from the new index.

Iterator state holds a pair of node references for current and successor coverage, lower and upper query bounds, start and end positions for hole versus used extents sharing storage, and a discriminator that distinguishes hole from used and terminated. Gap consolidation updates the current reference to the maximal reach among overlapping or contiguous successors.

Interval nodes carry inclusive start and inclusive end positions that define overlap and contiguity. Coverage queries treat touching extents where one end plus one equals the next start as a single merged run for gap purposes.
Two accessor macros select the start field and the end field of a node reference, providing shorthand for bound comparisons and extent propagation throughout span handling.

Test support defines a helper that declares a static configuration variable with module parameter exposure and description, plus globals for a cached tree root, a node array, a query array, and a deterministic random state used to synthesize endpoints and search positions.

Test helpers count overlaps for a query range, synthesize random intervals and query points within configured limits, measure insert plus remove cycles, measure search cycles with optional full range queries, and cross check tree iteration against linear bitmap marking over whole and random ranges with warnings on mismatch and allocation failure handling.

Maple adapter translates current maple position into span iterator extents by walking to the present location, clamping to query bounds, coalescing consecutive ranges of identical hole status up to the upper bound, writing the merged extent into hole or used fields, and positioning the maple cursor after the emitted extent unless overflow occurred.
Maple walk operation ensures lock checking and walkable state, then resolves the entry at the cursor while normalizing index and last positions for empty and pointer cases.

Walk handling retries when start status is observed, expands none status to the full index universe, and distinguishes a zero based single entry that returns directly from a non zero pointer case that yields empty with normalized bounds. Other statuses return the located entry unchanged.

Decoder construction fails cleanly on oversized header counts, unbuildable code length trees, length array overruns during repeat expansion, unbuildable literal or distance trees with diagnostic reporting, allocation exhaustion, and input exhaustion. Partial tables are released before returning, and a dedicated code distinguishes input shortage from malformed content.

Container validation rejects bad signatures, non deflate methods, encrypted or multipart or reserved flag use, malformed payloads with distinct diagnostics per failure class, checksum mismatch, length mismatch against observed output, and truncated input during header or trailer parsing.

Gap consolidation must track maximal reach rather than first reach, treat overlap and exact contiguity as merged, clamp emitted extents to the query upper bound, clear node references upon completion, and avoid underflow when computing one before a zero start or overflow when adding one to a maximal end.

Range checking allocates two bitmaps sized by node count and aborts the round with a warning when allocation fails, ensuring previously allocated storage is released. Iteration results are compared for equality with a one shot warning on divergence.
